hook.say: He did not say those years never happened | or did not matter. He *counted* them.

cues.text: And **I will restore to you the years** that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpiller, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you.
Three truths for every child who has lost years
He did not say those years | never happened. | *He counted them.*
Those years were real. | And it is *not your fault.*

cues.label: TRUTH 2 OF 3
cues.title: The Father Restores *By Sending His Son*

cues.text: He gave Himself — | the One who *is life.*
Bring the number | to the Father | who *sent His Son.*

cues.title: TODAY'S THREE TRUTHS
items: The Father restores by sending His Son

cues.text: The years that were lost | *can be gained.*
There is a God | who sent His Son, | *who is life.*

child.text: Write down seven good things God has given you this year. Read them quietly to God. Keep the list.

father.text: On paper, answer the question: how many years? Beside it, write one thing you missed in each year. Pray over it.

lines.text: Father, You are the One that restores years.
You came as a Son so that we can meet the Father. Show Yourself today.
Thank You, Holy Father. In the name of Jesus Christ.

cues.text: God is my Father, | and Jesus Christ is *my life.*

art.prompt: Night inside a small one-room home with deep teal walls. On the right third of the frame a small boy of about seven in a yellow shirt has fallen asleep sitting on the floor with his back against a closed wooden door, knees drawn up, his cheek resting on his folded arms, a plain steel wristwatch with a blank face on his small wrist. Beside him on the floor a single candle has burned down to a short stub and still glows warmly. Soft silver-blue moonlight falls through a small high window onto him like a gentle watching light. The mood is tender and peaceful; he is safe and seen. Large calm empty area of teal wall on the left.

Early morning at the edge of a West African village of round mud huts with thatched roofs. A tall man in a simple long cream robe, seen from behind so his face is not visible, walks slowly along a narrow earth path through a field of tall, heavy golden millet, holding the hand of a small boy of about seven in a yellow shirt who walks beside him and looks up at him. The low sun ahead of them pours warm golden rays through the millet heads and rims their shoulders. A few round thatched huts far away on the left. Deep teal sky fading to gold at the horizon, a large calm empty sky at the top.

Night inside a small one-room home with deep teal walls. On the right third of the frame a West African father in a green patterned shirt sits on a low wooden stool, leaning forward, holding a small child's steel wristwatch with a blank face in his open palm and looking down at it with quiet sorrow. Behind him, softly out of focus, his son of about seven in a yellow shirt sleeps peacefully on a woven mat under a cloth. A single candle on a small wooden table beside the father lights his face warmly. Large calm empty area of teal wall on the left.

trailer.say: The birthdays where you got no *wishes.* | The night of waiting for someone to come through the door.
Maybe your father took some *years* from you.
You stopped your watch, you stopped counting, | you stopped *caring.*

trailer.text: And **I will restore to you the years** that the locust hath eaten

trailer.say: He did not promise that those years would not happen. | He just promises you *Himself.*
Son, daughter, the years that were lost because your father wasn't there | can be *gained,* because you have Jesus Christ as your Father.

titles: God Sees The Years I Lost | Day 3 · The Father Showed Up
He Counted Them: For Every Child Who Lost Years
I Will Restore The Years: Joel 2:25 For Every Family
social.description:
Locusts can eat a whole farm in one afternoon, and some children have lost years the same way. God did not say those years never happened: He counted them, and He sent His Son to restore what was lost.

THE WORD: Joel 2:25 (read Joel 2:21–27 aloud)
TONIGHT, children: write down seven good things God has given you this year. Read them quietly to God. Keep the list.
TONIGHT, fathers: on paper, answer the question: how many years? Beside it, write one thing you missed in each year. Pray over it.
SAY IT: God saw every year. He gives me Himself.
